subject: Operations
title: Boeing 737 MAX Crashes
description: A 60-second lesson on Boeing 737 MAX Crashes.

hook.text: Two brand-new planes crashed within five months. 346 people died. Boeing's operations failures were systemic.

buildup.text: Boeing redesigned the 737 MAX with larger engines that changed flight characteristics. Software was added to compensate.

discovery.text: The MCAS software relied on a single sensor. When it failed, the system repeatedly pushed the nose down.

twist.text: Boeing pressured regulators, minimized pilot training, and hid the MCAS system's risks to speed certification.

climax.text: The MAX was grounded worldwide for nearly two years. Boeing lost $20 billion and its reputation for safety.

punchline.text: Speed-to-market killed people. Safety has no shortcut.

quiz.question: What software system caused the 737 MAX crashes?
